renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: locus_map
  title: Gene arrows along a contig
  description: |-
    Each arrow is a coding sequence, transfer RNA or ribosomal RNA placed on a contig of one bin, pointing in the direction of the gene and coloured by feature class. It answers how the genes of a bin are organised.
    How to read: pick one bin and one contig. Runs of arrows on one strand are operons, a switch of direction marks a strand change, and a cluster of ribosomal RNA arrows is the rRNA operon that decides the MIMAG tier of the bin.
    Note: Prokka renames contigs to internal identifiers, so the coordinates are valid within a bin only.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tseemann/prokka/master/README.md and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28787424/
  kind: gene_arrow_track
  roles:
    contig: contig
    feature_id: feature_id
    start: start
    end: end
    strand: strand
    class: ftype
    label: gene

- component: figure
  title: Feature length by class
  description: |-
    Each bar counts features in a length bin, one overlaid histogram per feature class. It answers whether the lengths of coding sequences, tRNAs and rRNAs look as expected.
    How to read: tRNAs are short, rRNAs long and coding sequences in between, so each class forms its own peak. A coding sequence peak shifted to short lengths points to fragmented genes in a poor assembly.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: length_bp
    color: ftype
    barmode: overlay
    opacity: 0.7
    labels:
      length_bp: Feature length (bp)
      ftype: Feature class

- component: card
  title: Annotated features
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of annotated features and the ring splits them by class (coding sequence, tRNA, rRNA); the second figure is the number of classes. It answers what the annotation is made of.
    How to read: coding sequences dominate, so look for the small RNA slices. A bin with no rRNA slice cannot reach the MIMAG high-quality tier.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28787424/
  column: ftype
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: ftype
  caption: features, by class

- component: card
  title: Feature length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median feature length in base pairs and the box shows the spread. It answers how long the typical annotated feature is.
    How to read: a very short median means fragmented genes. Filter to one class to read it for coding sequences only.
  column: length_bp
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: length, quartiles over features

- component: card
  title: Distinct gene products
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct gene product names and the second figure the count of features; the bars rank binners by distinct products. It answers how functionally diverse the annotation is.
    How to read: many features with few distinct products means mostly hypothetical proteins, common in uncharacterised bins.
  column: product
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: binner
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: distinct products, by binner

- component: table
  title: Annotated feature table
  description: |-
    Each row is a feature with its bin, contig, class, coordinates, strand, length, gene name and product. It answers which features lie where.
    How to read: filter by class or product, for example to list every tRNA of a bin.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: density_vs_size
  title: Coding density against bin size
  description: |-
    Each point is a bin: its size in base pairs and its number of coding sequences per megabase, sized by total coding sequences and coloured by the binner that produced it. It answers which bins annotate as plausible genomes.
    How to read: bins of similar density cluster together, and outliers are worth a look. Very low density in a large bin suggests missed genes or non-coding content; compare binners by their colour groups.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median coding density of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Prokka. Prokka and MIMAG publish no density cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tseemann/prokka/master/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Bin size (bp)
    y_title: Coding sequences per Mbp
    log_x: true
    legend_pos: bottom
    top_n_labels: 5
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: bases
    y: cds_per_mbp
    label: bin_id
    color: binner
    size: cds

- component: advanced_viz
  id: trna_vs_rrna
  title: tRNAs against rRNAs per bin
  description: |-
    Each point is a bin: its count of transfer RNAs and of ribosomal RNAs, sized by bin size and coloured by the assembler. It answers which bins carry the RNA genes of a high-quality draft.
    How to read: the MIMAG high-quality draft needs the 5S, 16S and 23S rRNA genes and at least 18 tRNAs, so look right of the line and at three or more rRNAs. Completeness alone cannot say this.
    Lines and annotations: the vertical line is the MIMAG minimum of 18 tRNAs. The rRNA requirement is one gene each of 5S, 16S and 23S, so a bin needs at least three rRNA features; the plot cannot tell which rRNA genes they are.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28787424/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Transfer RNAs
    y_title: Ribosomal RNAs
    reference_line: vertical
    reference_value: 18
    reference_label: MIMAG, at least 18 tRNAs
    legend_pos: bottom
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: trna
    y: rrna
    label: bin_id
    color: assembler
    size: bases

- component: figure
  title: Gene density per assembler
  description: |-
    Each bar counts bins in a coding density bin, one overlaid histogram per assembler. It answers whether an assembler yields bins with systematically fewer annotated genes.
    How to read: histograms centred on the same value mean comparable annotation. A shifted one points to fragmented genes from that assembler.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median coding density of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Prokka.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: cds_per_mbp
    color: assembler
    barmode: overlay
    opacity: 0.6
    labels:
      cds_per_mbp: Coding sequences per Mbp
      assembler: Assembler
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: median
    column: cds_per_mbp

- component: card
  title: Coding sequences
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of coding sequences over the bins in view and the bar splits it by binner. It answers which binner contributes most of the annotated genes.
    How to read: a large share is partly a matter of how many bins the binner produced, so read it with the bin count card.
  column: cds
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: binner
  caption: coding sequences, by binner

- component: card
  title: Coding density
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of coding sequences per megabase and the box shows the spread. It answers how gene-dense the bins are.
    How to read: a box far from the others, or a very low median, signals bins with missed genes or large non-coding content. Prokka and MIMAG publish no density cut-off.
  column: cds_per_mbp
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: density, quartiles over bins

- component: card
  title: Transfer RNAs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of tRNAs per bin, compared with the MIMAG minimum of 18 for a high-quality draft. It answers whether bins carry enough tRNA genes.
    How to read: below 18 a bin cannot reach the high-quality tier. Open the scatter to see which bins fall short.
    Lines and annotations: the threshold is the MIMAG minimum of 18 tRNAs.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28787424/
  column: trna
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 18.0
  threshold_direction: min
  caption: median against the MIMAG minimum of 18

- component: card
  title: Ribosomal RNAs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest count of rRNA features in a bin and the histogram shows the distribution over bins. It answers how many bins have any rRNA at all.
    How to read: a bin with no rRNA feature cannot reach the high-quality tier. That tier needs the 5S, 16S and 23S genes, so a bin needs at least three rRNA features.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28787424/
  column: rrna
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - q3
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: rRNAs, distribution over bins

- component: card
  title: Annotated bins
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of annotated bins and the second figure the number of assemblers; the bars rank assemblers by bins. It answers how the bins are spread over assemblers.
    How to read: an assembler with few bins may simply have produced few usable ones, so compare with the density and RNA tiles.
  column: assembler
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: assembler
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: bins, by assembler

- component: table
  title: Bin annotation table
  description: |-
    Each row is a bin with its assembler, binner, contigs, bases, coding sequences, tRNAs, rRNAs, tmRNAs and whether it meets the MIMAG RNA criteria. It answers which bins pass the annotation half of the high-quality standard.
    How to read: sort by tRNA or rRNA count, and check the MIMAG column. It is empty when the GFF, which names the rRNA genes, was not provided.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28787424/
